subject: Data retention carveout: 7-day KV/log window proposal for FinHealth
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap and next steps from today — data handling & retention

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the time to talk today. Quick recap to make sure we're aligned and to capture requested follow-ups: 

- Call attendees: Aisha (FinHealth), Ravi (FinHealth ops), Lauren (Redwood Sales), Jonas (Redwood Security).
- Key ask: FinHealth needs a narrow retention carveout for PII-containing inference logs tied to a pilot scope. Prefer short window (7 days) for KV/cache and request option for zero-persist on certain endpoints.
- Must-haves you mentioned: encrypted-at-rest, customer-managed keys (KMS), an auditable deletion path, and written amendment for procurement.

Action items we captured: 
1) Redwood to propose an operational approach for a 7-day retention window and call out which artifacts would still exist (access logs, metrics, aggregated billing tokens).
2) Security to send SOC2 summary and redacted evidence we can include in your procurement package.
3) Legal/Contracts to draft a short amendment covering the retention schedule and deletion SLA for the pilot.

I'll loop in Marissa (security) and Jonas (eng) for the technical details. Attached a one-pager matrix outlining options (short window, zero-persist, per-endpoint opt-out) to get us started.

Proposed next steps: Marissa to share technical constraints and a recommended config by EOD Monday, and our agreements team will surface a draft amendment the following week.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag. Otherwise we'll proceed.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Attachments: data_retention_matrix.csv

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@finhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps from today — data handling & retention

Thanks Lauren — that's accurate. A couple clarifying points from our side: 

- The 7-day window we'd like to confirm applies to any stored KV/cache and full request/response logs that could include patient identifiers. We still want aggregated metrics/usage for billing/observability but with no way to reconstruct PII after 7 days.
- For the zero-persist option: we only need it for our triage endpoint where we expect very sensitive tokens; will need clear runbooks for correlation/debugging when logs are disabled.
- Procurement asked whether the deletion can be triggered via API/console and for a signed certificate of destruction for records older than 7 days.

Can Marissa confirm whether Redwood can: a) enforce per-endpoint retention, b) provide deletion certificates, and c) support CMK (customer-managed key) with our KMS provider?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Aisha
Director, InfoSec | FinHealth Inc
aisha.khan@finhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps from today — data handling & retention

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the notes — quick answers below plus attached artifacts. 

1) Per-endpoint retention: Yes. Our platform supports per-route retention policies. For the pilot we can scope the triage endpoint to a zero-persist mode (no persistent request/response logs; only ephemeral in-memory KV for the duration of the inference request) and keep diagnostic sampling off by default. We will document driver/agent behaviors so your SREs know how to reproduce issues when logs are off.

2) 7-day KV/log window: For endpoints that require retention, we can configure an automated TTL process that truncates full-text logs and purges KV cache 7 days after creation. Note: short windows reduce debugging fidelity; we recommend keeping 24-hour rolling short traces for error correlation for the first week of the pilot and then enabling the strict 7-day purge.

3) Deletion certificate: We can provide an automated deletion report (signed by our system) showing object ids and timestamps for purged artifacts. For procurement purposes we can export a PDF certificate for a given date range.

4) CMK/KMS: We support AWS KMS/Google KMS customers for Private deployments and can integrate CMK with our private tenant key policies. For hosted pilots we can support envelope encryption with a customer-supplied master key; full HSM integration requires Private deployment conversation.

Attached: redacted_SOC2_summary.pdf and a detailed data_retention_matrix.csv that maps artifact types to retention behavior.

Proposed technical config for pilot:
- Triage endpoint: zero-persist mode, request-level ephemeral KV only; explicit runbook for debug escalation.
- Clinical ingest endpoints: 7-day retention for full logs + automated purge job; 24-hour short traces retained for 7 days only for first 7 days.
- Deletion certificate generated weekly and on-demand via API.

We'll also draft a short amendment (proposed_amendment_FH_7day.docx) for procurement. Expect a first draft by Tue (our legal team). Happy to set a 30-min technical review once you've had a look.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redacted_SOC2_summary.pdf, data_retention_matrix.csv

From: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps from today — data handling & retention

Marissa — the technical config looks reasonable. A couple of ops questions: 

- How will deletion certificates be authenticated? We need something we can archive in our compliance system — signed PDF is fine but will need a digest or signature we can verify.
- What does "ephemeral in-memory KV" mean for our scaling? Will we see increased memory pressure during high QPS? Any recommended limits or rate-limiting knobs?

If you can include short notes on verification of deletion certs and memory/throughput considerations in the technical review that would help our SREs sign off.

Thanks,
Ravi
FinHealth Ops

If that timeline works I'll mark the next actions as committed and open a HubSpot task for the draft amendment.

Thanks — Lauren
